answer: One strong defence is stake-backed reputation: an agent must lock a refundable deposit and earn trust only through verified completed work, so each identity carries real cost. A flood of fake identities then looks like a plume of smoke, noisy but thin, because no single signal of quality, such as repeated successful deliveries, can be faked cheaply at scale. Like a lotus rooted in mud yet rising clean, genuine reputation grows slowly from proven history, while Sybil clones wither because buying, staking and maintaining each copy costs more than any reward it can extract.
